queries.text: I dreaded speaking in front of my coworkers this week. My pulse sped up beforehand, and I kept imagining that I would embarrass myself.

candidates.text: Knowing the directors would assess my proposal made me practice every sentence late into the night.
During the hiring panel, I lost my train of thought and worried afterward that I had made a fool of myself.
At the company gathering, my voice trembled when everyone turned toward me, even though I knew what I wanted to say.
I spent a peaceful afternoon pruning the tomato plants and watering the herbs.
I had lunch with two colleagues and enjoyed hearing about their weekend trips.
I finally found a clean color palette for the slides and aligned all the charts before sending the deck.
I ran up the hill by the reservoir and my heartbeat stayed high for several minutes afterward.
I knocked over my mug in the kitchen and felt silly cleaning the mess while my roommate watched.
The report deadline moved up, so I reorganized the week and finished the analysis before Friday.
I signed up for a community storytelling class because I want to learn how to hold an audience's attention.

queries.text: Even after several weeks in this city, I still feel like an outsider. Weekends are especially hard because I have nobody nearby to call or make plans with.

candidates.text: Saturday dragged on. I walked around streets I don't recognize and wished I had someone here to share an ordinary day with.
I ate dinner by myself again and missed the easy company I used to have around the table back home.
The cafe was full of groups who seemed to know one another. I felt invisible and longed for a familiar face.
I unpacked the last kitchen boxes, labeled the storage bins, and finally found a place for the winter coats.
I figured out which bus gets me to the office fastest and saved the route in my phone.
My friend from college called for my birthday. We laughed about our old apartment and caught up on work.
The farmers market was packed, so I bought apples quickly and left before the afternoon rush.
My new role has a steep learning curve, but the team explained the tools and I finished my first assignment.
I stayed home with a sore throat, drank ginger tea, and watched a documentary about deep-sea fish.
I spent the afternoon at the design museum and found a tiny bookstore on the walk back.

queries.text: I stayed on my phone long after bedtime several nights. The next mornings I felt drained, foggy, and unusually short-tempered.

candidates.text: I kept watching short clips until almost 2 a.m. and could barely focus when the alarm rang.
I refreshed the news and social feeds in bed for ages; by breakfast I felt heavy-headed and impatient with everyone.
One more game turned into several, and I dragged myself through the first half of the following day.
I read a few chapters of a paperback, put it down at ten, and woke up refreshed before my alarm.
A fever and aching joints kept me in bed most of the day; I canceled my plans and drank plenty of water.
The train was delayed, and I arrived at the office annoyed after standing on the platform in the rain.
I used my phone to photograph the changing leaves in the park and shared a few pictures with my sister.
I had a strong coffee after lunch and felt jittery during the afternoon planning meeting.
The 5 a.m. flight meant getting up before dawn, but I slept well the previous night and napped after landing.
A gentle stretch class helped me unwind after work, and I was ready to turn in soon afterward.
